interpretationRules: ROR measures disproportionality of reporting in FAERS, not clinical risk, incidence, or causality. FAERS analyses are hypothesis-generating.
Aprocitentan rows are sentinel and exploratory only, cohort n = 17.

Finerenone hyperkalemia has two different estimates that must never be merged: 5.47 versus global background and 0.68 head-to-head versus spironolactone. The QA sheet attributes the paradox to a background artifact.

relatedEstimatesNotInRows.note: Global background ROR from abstract and script. Included only to disambiguate the finerenone endocrine block. Not one of the five requested rows.

Head-to-head odds ratio from the presentation script, equal to 87 percent lower reporting odds, p < 0.001. This is the source of the poster EVIDENCE panel minus 87 percent figure. It is not the global ROR 1.03.
Head-to-head ROR from abstract and script, p = 0.017, uncorrected for multiple testing per the QA sheet. Its lower CI bound 0.50 is a plausible source of confusion with the poster ARNI 0.50 value.

rows.comparator: Global background (all other reports in the analysis set)
rows.evidence: Poster SO WHAT panel: finerenone, no endocrine signal, ROR 1.03. Abstract Results: spironolactone endocrine ROR 10.85, finerenone no endocrine signal ROR 1.03. Presentation script: ROR 1.03, 95 percent CI 0.54 to 1.99, CI crossing one.
rows.gap: Event-case count for finerenone endocrine events is not stated in the poster, abstract, script, or QA sheet. The poster block also contains a different estimate, the head-to-head endocrine odds ratio 0.13 (CI 0.06 to 0.28, p < 0.001, 87 percent lower reporting odds versus spironolactone). Do not confuse that 0.13 with the global ROR 1.03.

rows.comparator: Global background (all other reports in the analysis set)
rows.evidence: Poster SO WHAT panel: ARNI, orthostatic hypotension, ROR 6.06, median onset 68 days. Abstract Results: sacubitril/valsartan orthostatic hypotension signal ROR 6.06, median onset 68 days. Presentation script: ROR 6.06, 95 percent CI 5.06 to 7.24.
rows.gap: Event-case count for ARNI orthostatic hypotension is not stated in the poster, abstract, script, or QA sheet.

rows.comparator: Global background (all other reports in the analysis set)
rows.evidence: Poster SO WHAT panel: aprocitentan, exploratory n = 17, edema, delayed onset, no electrolyte signal, ROR 9.00. Abstract Results: aprocitentan peripheral edema signal ROR 9.00, strictly sentinel and exploratory with wide confidence intervals. Presentation script: ROR 9.00, 95 percent CI 3.31 to 24.46, wide, reflecting only 17 reports.
rows.gap: Total edema event-case count is not stated in the available documents. The script notes the time-to-onset median of 152 days for aprocitentan edema rests on only 3 cases with valid dates. That 3 is a time-to-onset subset, not the total edema case count, so it is not used as cases here. This row must always be labeled sentinel and exploratory.

rows.comparator: Global background (all other reports in the analysis set)
rows.evidence: Drug, outcome, and comparator are proven. Poster SO WHAT panel: finerenone hyperkalemia ROR 5.47 vs background, monitor serum K+. Presentation script: finerenone hyperkalemia ROR 5.47 against the global background, contrasted with 0.68 head-to-head against spironolactone, described as a background artifact.
rows.gap: No 95 percent CI for ROR 5.47 appears in the poster, abstract, presentation script, or QA sheet, and no hyperkalemia event-case count for finerenone appears either. The QA sheet proves a manuscript Table 2 exists (it cites a finerenone renal signal ROR 4.60 with 396 cases from Table 2), but that manuscript and table are not in the goal folder. Obtain Table 2 before publishing this row with a CI or a case count.

rows.evidence: Only the poster prints this value, in the ARNI block as lower hyperkalemia reporting (ROR 0.50). It appears identically in both the v3 poster and the v3 asterisk variant.
rows.gap: No corroboration in the abstract, presentation script, or QA sheet, and no CI or case count anywhere in the goal folder. Worse, 0.50 also appears as the lower confidence bound of a different estimate, the head-to-head hyperkalemia ROR 0.68 (CI 0.50 to 0.93, p = 0.017) for finerenone versus spironolactone. Until manuscript Table 2 is checked, ROR 0.50 cannot be trusted as a standalone ARNI hyperkalemia estimate and must not be plotted.

source.analysisSet: 7,519 FAERS reports retrieved, 2-stage dedup to N = 6,601 unique reports. Background set n = 3,279.
source.tableOrSection: Poster, 1 slide 16:9, panels EVIDENCE and SO WHAT. Supporting sources in the same folder: Lecture-Abstract-ABST-000034-DRAFT.pdf, naskah-presentasi-7-menit-ABST-000034.docx, lembar-QA-poster-ABST-000034.md.

summary: 3 of 5 ROR values are mapped to drug, outcome, comparator, and 95 percent CI from the poster plus the abstract and the 7-minute presentation script. 2 of 5 rows are unverified: finerenone hyperkalemia ROR 5.47 has no CI in any available document, and sacubitril/valsartan hyperkalemia ROR 0.50 appears only on the poster with no corroboration. No row has a proven event-case count, because the manuscript Table 2 is not present in the goal folder, so every cases value is null. Do not render this file as a finished forest plot until the gaps below are closed.
